name: Siena
title: Holidays in Siena
intro: A medieval Tuscan city built around a shell-shaped piazza, famous for its bareback horse race and striped Gothic cathedral. Here's what Siena is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Siena's cathedral and red-brick houses on their hilltop
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April to June and September to October are best, warm and good for countryside drives. The Palio horse race takes place on 2 July and 16 August, when the city is packed. July and August are hot. Winter is quiet and cool.

things.name: Piazza del Campo
things.blurb: The sloping, shell-shaped main square, perfect for sitting on the bricks.

things.name: Siena Cathedral
things.blurb: Black-and-white striped marble, inlaid floors and the frescoed Piccolomini Library.

things.name: Torre del Mangia
things.blurb: Climb the tall tower over the Campo for a view of the rooftops.

things.name: Palio
things.blurb: Watch the frantic horse race round the Campo, or the trial races in the days before.

things.name: San Gimignano
things.blurb: The town of medieval towers, about an hour away.

things.name: Val d'Orcia
things.blurb: Rolling hills, cypress trees and the wine towns of Montalcino and Montepulciano.

faqs.question: Is Siena worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's one of the best-preserved medieval cities in Italy and much calmer than Florence, especially in the evening.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Siena?
faqs.answer: Two days covers the city. Use it as a base for three or four to see San Gimignano and the Val d'Orcia.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Siena?
faqs.answer: April to June and September, around 19 to 28°C. Book far ahead for the Palio in July and August.

faqs.question: How do you get to Siena?
faqs.answer: Fly into Florence or Pisa, both with direct flights from the UK, then take the bus from Florence, about 1 hour 15 minutes.

faqs.question: Siena or Florence?
faqs.answer: Florence has more famous art, but Siena is smaller, quieter and easier to enjoy at a slow pace. Many people visit both.
